analysis.one_liner: Apollo Hospitals runs one of India's largest hospital chains along with a pharmacy network, diagnostics business and a digital health platform (Apollo 24/7).
tags: Demerger of digital biz pending (Q4 FY27)
analysis.whats_happening: Q2 FY27 results (reported Nov 4, 2026) showed revenue up 23% YoY to ₹7,615 crore and PAT up 32% to ₹630 crore, with occupancy rising to 73% from 69%. Separately, the government's drug pricing regulator (NPPA) capped trade margins at 30% on 137 anti-cancer drug formulations effective November 9, 2026, which matters because oncology is roughly a fifth of revenue for large hospital chains. The long-planned demerger of the digital/pharmacy business (AHLL, Apollo 24/7 and Keimed) into a separately listed entity has NCLT and shareholder approval but is still pending, with management guiding to a listing in Q4 FY27 (Jan-Mar 2027) and no record date announced yet.
analysis.plain_terms: This is a hospital company bundled with a pharmacy chain, a diagnostics arm and a loss-making-turned-breakeven online health app, which makes it harder to value than a pure hospital business. The core hospital business is growing well on both patients treated and margins, which is the healthier kind of growth. But a chunk of the group (digital plus pharmacy distribution) is being carved out into a new company that isn't trading yet, so today's share price reflects a business that is about to change shape. On top of that, a fresh government cap on cancer-drug margins lands right after results, adding a near-term question mark on the pharmacy side.
analysis.quarters: Revenue and profit have accelerated through FY27: Q1 FY27 revenue was up ~21% YoY with EBITDA margin at 15.5%, and Q2 FY27 revenue rose 23% YoY with EBITDA margin expanding further to 15.64% from 14.93% a year earlier, and PAT up 32% YoY. For H1 FY27 overall, revenue was up 22% and PAT up 33%. Importantly, the growth rode on both occupancy (73% vs 69%) and bed additions (+5.9% to 8,522 beds), not just pricing. The digital arm (Apollo 24/7) swung from a loss to a small cash profit, and AHLL's EBITDA margin rose to 14.3% from 9.5%, with AHLL posting a ₹26 crore profit versus a ₹4 crore loss a year ago - both are margin-led turnarounds within smaller segments rather than the core driver of group growth. Newer hospitals (Gurugram, Sonarpur, Financial District Hyderabad, Sarjapur) are still ramping and together dragged ~₹35 crore in losses this quarter.
analysis.performance_read: The stock is down 6.9% from its September 23, 2026 peak but this is a mild pullback, not a crash - it remains well above its 52-week low of ₹6,776.6 and close to its 52-week high of ₹9,069. The only corporate action in the stock's history is a 2010 stock split (already reflected in prices), so none of the long-term return numbers need adjustment for spin-offs. Over 1 and 3 years the stock has beaten both the Nifty and peer Max Healthcare (1Y: +8.8% vs Nifty -1.88% and peer -16.86%; 3Y: +65.68% vs Nifty +28.98% and peer +57.06%). But over 5 years Apollo's +94.34% trails Max Healthcare's +176.94% by a wide margin, so the recent outperformance is a reversal of a longer period of lagging the peer.
analysis.valuation_read: Apollo trades at roughly 53-54x trailing earnings, cheaper than Max Healthcare (~71x) and Fortis (~64x) on that measure, but more expensive on price-to-book (~11.4x vs ~9.4x and ~6.6x respectively) - the two metrics disagree because Apollo's blended business (hospitals, pharmacy, diagnostics, digital) carries a different earnings mix than the peers' purer hospital models. Its EV/EBITDA of roughly 34x is actually about 30% below its own 3-year average of ~47x, suggesting the market has partly de-rated it, plausibly reflecting uncertainty around the pending demerger and the fresh oncology-drug margin cap rather than a view that the hospital business itself is cheap.
analysis.growth_read: Growth is currently both volume-led and margin-led, which is the more durable combination: occupancy rose to 73% from 69% and operating beds grew 5.9%, while EBITDA margin simultaneously expanded to 15.64% from 14.93%. The digital and AHLL segments are improving mainly through margin expansion off a small base (AHLL margin 9.5% to 14.3%; digital arm loss to small cash profit) rather than large revenue gains, so their contribution to group growth is still modest in absolute rupee terms.
analysis.health_read: EBITDA margins are expanding and the ₹7,100 crore, roughly 5,800-bed five-year capacity expansion is being funded through internal accruals rather than new borrowing, per management, with reported debt/equity near 0.85x. Not verified - check on Screener for the actual operating cash flow and free cash flow figures to confirm how much of this profit growth is converting to cash; that detail wasn't available from current sources. The nearer-term risk looks more operational than financial: new hospitals (Gurugram, Sonarpur, Financial District Hyderabad, Sarjapur) are running at a combined loss while ramping up, and the new NPPA margin cap on cancer drugs adds a fresh pressure point on the pharmacy/oncology revenue line.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoter holding (the Reddy family, largely via PCR Investments Ltd) stands at 28.02% and has been stable. Promoter pledging has been cut sharply, from around 13% to about 2.49% of promoter holding, after a stake sale used to pay down debt - a meaningful reduction in that specific financial risk. Foreign institutional holding has risen to 43.18% from 41.49% in the prior quarter, while domestic institutional holding eased slightly to 22.07% from 24%, and mutual fund holding is roughly stable near 17%. No single marquee individual investor stands out on the shareholder register beyond routine institutional and promoter-family holdings.
strengths: Q2 FY27 revenue up 23% YoY to ₹7,615 crore with EBITDA margin expanding to 15.64% from 14.93% - growth paired with margin gains, not one at the expense of the other
Occupancy rose to 73% from 69% and operating beds grew 5.9% to 8,522, showing genuine demand-led volume growth rather than pricing alone

Digital arm Apollo 24/7 turned cash-positive in Q2 FY27 versus a ₹39 crore loss a year earlier, and AHLL's EBITDA margin rose to 14.3% from 9.5% with PAT of ₹26 crore versus a ₹4 crore loss a year ago
Promoter pledge cut from roughly 13% to about 2.49% of promoter holding, reducing a specific source of financial-stress risk
watchpoints: NPPA capped trade margins at 30% on 137 anti-cancer drug formulations effective November 9, 2026; oncology is roughly a fifth of revenue for large hospital chains, so this is a direct margin risk to watch in coming quarters

The demerger of AHLL, Apollo 24/7 and Keimed into a separately listed entity has NCLT and shareholder approval but no confirmed record date or share-swap ratio yet, with management targeting a Q4 FY27 (Jan-Mar 2027) listing - this is still a pending event, not a completed one

Newer hospitals (Gurugram, Sonarpur, Financial District Hyderabad, Sarjapur) posted a combined ~₹35 crore loss in Q2 FY27 while ramping up, and a further ₹7,100 crore, ~5,800-bed expansion is planned over five years
The stock's 5-year return of 94.34% trails peer Max Healthcare's 176.94% by a wide margin, even though Apollo has outperformed over the more recent 1-year and 3-year periods
analysis.one_thing: The actual listing of Apollo Healthtech (the merged AHLL + Apollo 24/7 + Keimed entity), expected in Q4 FY27 - its record date, share-swap ratio and standalone profitability will clarify how much of today's valuation belongs to the hospital business versus the digital/pharmacy business.
analysis.data_notes: Q2 and Q1 FY27 revenue, EBITDA, PAT and occupancy figures were cross-checked across multiple financial news sources and were consistent; minor rounding differences exist across sources for exact EBITDA (₹1,190-1,191 crore) and digital cash profit (₹1-1.3 crore) figures. The demerger timeline (NCLT order May 5, 2026; shareholder approval June 24, 2026; targeted Q4 FY27 listing) was corroborated by management's Nov 5, 2026 earnings call commentary. Not verified: exact free cash flow/operating cash flow conversion, the next quarter's results date, and the next dividend record date - none were confirmed from available sources, so check Screener or the company's exchange filings directly for these.
